prompt:
Create ONE 1672x941 wide luxury fashion-editorial photograph by refining reference 1. This is SIG-COMMERCE-1, the Signature Sherpa-and-beanie shopping scene.
REFERENCE ROLES: Reference 1 is the locked cast, outfit, existing terrace layout and Golden Gate scene. Reference 2 is the NATURAL PHOTOGRAPHIC INTEGRATION BENCHMARK only: emulate how its models, sunset/sky light, wet stone and contact shadows belong to one photographed space. Never import any of its people, shirts, printed shorts, pastel set, poses, or SR monogram sculpture. Reference 3 is the EXACT SKYYROSE FONT SCULPTURE to introduce. Reference 4 shows the existing Signature collection hero world. Use that hero's materials and the referenced font statue, not an invented wordmark.
PRESERVE: The exact original sole man in reference 1: same face, age, skin tone, mustache, gaze, small-patch black beanie, hairstyle, hands-in-pockets pose, body proportions, jacket folds, black trousers and black/white sneakers. His jacket retains the actual smooth black Sherpa exterior, cream collar/lining and exact existing small red rose/cloud chest emblem, zipper, seams, pockets and length. Do not replace the beanie patch, enlarge/redraw the emblem, alter the jacket into a furry coat, invent sleeve graphics, recast the model or modify his pose. Preserve the same Golden Gate overlook, bridge/cable design on the right, city on the left, dark wet stone terraces, actual steps, gold strip lights, camera and depth arrangement. No unrelated concrete venue, new bridge type or replacement architecture.
PRIMARY TASK: It must no longer look like an isolated studio man pasted onto a terrace. Render the scene as one sophisticated in-camera fashion photograph with the believable physical integration achieved by reference 2. Model scale and lens perspective should agree with the stone steps and distant bridge. Place the same unchanged figure on a genuinely level foreground stone landing, with BOTH soles on a single physical horizontal plane; shift the intact figure minimally if required to move it off the vertical stair riser. Never invent a slab glued under his shoes or float him above a step. Keep his original stance. Preserve all body anatomy and shoes.
LIGHT: Hero-consistent late sunset transitioning into blue hour. A large soft warm-neutral key motivated by the sky/sunset gently illuminates face, cream collar and front emblem; cooler sky fill opens black fabric detail; only a narrow restrained warm rim on sunset-facing edges. Light direction, exposure, color temperature, black levels and grain must agree across the man and his surroundings. Remove the studio-bright outline and flat front lighting. Preserve nuanced real skin and rich black fabric, avoiding washed-out or crushed tones. The garment stays sharply readable without looking artificially spotlit. Match edge sharpness, fine hair detail and local contrast to the optical environment, not blur the person.
GROUNDING: Tight shoe-shaped contact occlusion, natural heel/toe weight, coherent soft cast shadow across the actual horizontal paving. Reflections must be low-opacity, irregular, broken by wet-stone roughness and continuous with the same light sources, not a perfect flipped duplicate, not black oval drop shadows. A small amount of bounced gold light from real terrace strips can touch the appropriate low-facing shoe/cloth surfaces. Thin distant bay mist belongs BEHIND the model, not in front of his face, emblem or feet. No glow outline or fog used to hide pasted edges.
FONT STATUE: Place reference 3's exact elegant joined gold SkyyRose calligraphy with its integrated rose in the right middle-ground on a substantial low black-stone plinth that stands naturally on the existing terrace. Preserve the actual letterforms, joined flourishes, integrated rose shape, gold/rose-gold finish and proportions. It reads SkyyRose, not SkyRose, not a substitute typeface. Do not add THE or COLLECTION, do not replace it with a generic SR monogram, and do not carry over reference 3's image background as a rectangular panel. It is physically three-dimensional freestanding metal, not floating overlay typography or a billboard. Show real sculpture thickness, sensible structural support through the base, contact shadow and restrained gold reflection on adjacent wet stone. Monument has believable scale, lower than the man, and remains clearly secondary to the clothing and face. Keep the full statue within frame, behind/right of the man with clean separation from his silhouette. Do not cover the Golden Gate's principal tower or obstruct the shopping look. Light it from the SAME sunset and sky, not its own studio.
Overall: poised natural campaign presence, tactile cloth, coherent depth, realistic skin, restrained filmic highlight rolloff, no overprocessed HDR. Keep negative space, full body, readable product. No new cast, changed clothes, extra props, glitter, thick smoke, strong vignette, lens flare, orange/teal wash or generic luxury lobby. The requested change is physical integration plus the exact hero-font statue, not new product design.

Create ONE 1672x941 wide cinematic fashion-shopping editorial photograph by refining reference 1, the Signature mint/lavender duo. The request is for a visibly more NATURAL, PHYSICALLY COHERENT scene that matches the realism and warm human photographic presence of reference 2.
REFERENCE RULES: reference 1 locks the two actual models, their looks, positions and the existing Golden Gate terrace environment. Reference 2 is solely the successful NATURAL INTEGRATION / LIGHT / CONTACT / REALISM BENCHMARK: do not borrow its three cast members, bridge-print clothes, pastel windbreaker, poses or monogram statue. Reference 3 anchors the original Signature hero world. The gold font statue will be in the companion Sherpa scene, NOT in this image. Do not add new lettering, statues or props here.
LOCKED SUBJECTS: Exactly the same two adults from reference 1: the man left, his actual face, cornrow hairstyle, skin tone, gaze to his right and relaxed hands-in-pockets stance; the woman right, her actual face, medium-brown skin, curly hair, gaze and relaxed stance. Retain body proportions and anatomy, not a reshaped figure or beautified replacement person. Keep the same facial identities, hairstyles, expressions, clothing fit and standing poses. Render them with living, nuanced skin and optical texture rather than plastic retouching.
EXACT WARDROBE: man keeps the original mint SG-013 CREWNECK sweatshirt (NOT a hoodie) and matching SG-014 mint full-length sweatpants, the exact gray/lavender rose/cloud graphics at the same chest and trouser positions, actual drawstring/waist details, cuffs, seams, folds and white sneakers. Woman keeps the original mint SG-006 LONG HOODIE DRESS with the same mid-thigh hem and loose silhouette, white drawstrings, real kangaroo pocket, lavender rose/cloud chest artwork, sleeve cuffs, BARE LEGS and the same white sneakers. Never put trousers/leggings underneath, never shorten into a normal hoodie, never change the rose artwork or mint/lavender colorway. Keep the original garment geometry and detailed graphics. No new jewelry, bags or unrelated logos.
ENVIRONMENT: preserve reference 1's Golden Gate lateral terrace, same exact bridge structures/cables, bay, fog-softened skyline, blue-gray sky and warm horizon, same dark wet stone terraces and gold inset step edges. Maintain the same scene layout and original camera. It should remain this specific Signature hero-inspired setting, not replace it with reference 2's courtyard. No rebuilt stairs, generic luxury plaza, different bridge or changed city.
NATURAL INTEGRATION, THE ESSENTIAL CHANGE: Bring the duo into one coherent photographic exposure with the same physically credible handling that makes reference 2 feel real. Eliminate the man's strong orange studio side light and the woman's separate flatter studio illumination; reconcile them under the actual sunset and sky so light direction, softness, falloff and contrast agree across the models and the paving. Use a large, soft warm-neutral late-day key to gently shape faces and garment fronts, cool open-sky fill to preserve dimension, and a restrained warm edge only on sunset-facing contours. Keep genuine mint and lavender, white sneakers and healthy skin, not a global teal/orange tint. Faces and product artwork form the focal hierarchy; no beauty-light hotspot detached from the setting. Preserve the same apparent individual expressions but make their shared spatial presence feel as natural as people photographed together on the terrace.
FLOOR CONTACT: Every existing sneaker must visibly sit with weight on its actual horizontal stone landing. The two people may remain on their respective terrace levels. If the old placement floats over a vertical riser, move that SAME intact figure a small amount to the nearby supporting horizontal tread without reshaping legs, changing pose, creating a fake slab or rebuilding architecture. Keep both models full-length with uncropped shoes. Tight individual sole/heel contact shadows; soft directional cast shadows consistent with the same key light; actual local occlusion. Wet-paving reflections are restrained, broken and roughened, anchored at shoe contact and attenuating across the correct floor plane. No generic dark oval shadow, doubled feet, reflected body ghosts or a crisp mirror person. Gold edge lights give subtle local floor bounce, not an artificial glow around silhouettes.
EDGE AND OPTICAL COHERENCE: hair flyaways and cloth contours must have natural edge detail and correct environmental spill, with no white cutout fringe or rubbery smoothing. Match skin/fabric acuity, microcontrast and subtle grain to the same lens and scene. Dimensional sleeves, waist folds and leg shading must respond to the light; no flat uniformly lit torsos. Avoid simply darkening the people to hide the mismatch. Preserve readable product contrast.
ATMOSPHERE: low bay haze behind the subjects only, with real separation of near stone, midground railing/terraces and far bridge. Keep the faces, artwork, long-dress hem, bare legs and shoes entirely clear. Let reflected sky and existing warm practicals tie surrounding floor to the bodies; no fog curtain in front. Cinematic, shoppable, human and tactile rather than a glossy catalog cutout. No strong vignette, lens flare, glitter, drifting petals, extra props, new background sculpture, added text, oversaturation or fantasy beams. The goal is for the existing mint duo to look naturally photographed at this location with the quality of reference 2, while retaining the locked people, looks and environment.
